decision: Use TypeScript and native DOM for a reusable observation panel. Keep the validated presenter and host-owned transport/refresh boundary. Add no rendering framework or runtime dependency.
constraints: Read-only aggregate display; current state always UNKNOWN, no identifiers or raw scene.
Explicit refresh and disposal; stable native controls; English and Swedish contextual guidance available without network.
Host must supply an exclusively owned root and fresh SDK view reader, enforce authorization, and schedule expiry refreshes. No scheduler or freshness claim is supplied by the renderer.

alternatives.assessment: Selected for this fixed three-state panel: DOM typings and existing versioned view types, textContent, native disclosure/buttons and explicit synchronous lifetime without an additional runtime. Choice is scoped to this panel, not the complete future operator application.
Equivalent runtime available; static DOM and locale contracts would require separate checked annotations/declarations. TypeScript preserves those checks without extra deployed runtime.

Provides reactive web components and declarative templates. Credible for a growing reusable design system; this fixed panel needs neither custom-element registration nor reactive scheduling. No demonstrated capability gain for its current size.

Typed messages and JS ports are credible for an application. The host SDK reader still needs interop and runtime validation; no performance or safety advantage has been established for this small synchronous DOM boundary.

Typed JavaScript interop remains a credible alternative. Native DOM bindings can express this component, but do not remove host trust or freshness responsibilities; no material runtime improvement established.

Development-only structural DOM testing, lock-pinned. Selected over hand-written DOM mocks to exercise actual tree creation/events; its documented non-browser scope prevents treating these tests as keyboard, screen-reader or layout qualification.

limits: No complete operator app, authentication, role enforcement, Help Center search, release-bound help inventory or P19 acceptance.
DOM structural tests do not establish actual browser, assistive-technology or customer-install acceptance. Local browser probes timed out.
No measured real-time latency, MLS/CNSA, DDS/Link16, five-nines, hardware or tactical deployment claim.
The host must refresh on every SDK display callback and relevant UI activation. Stalled host execution can leave delayed historical text visible; current conditions always remain UNKNOWN.
Caller-controlled functions and DOM are trusted in-process integration; this is not an isolation boundary.
